page.layout: One printed page of running text in one column, with marginal notes in the left margin (year and reference notes) and the right margin. Page number 644 at head top left; running head "Anastasius Dicorus" centred; "Lib. III. A.C." at top right.

main_text.l: cuiquam militem fieri, nili is tribus teftibus, se,
Christianum esse probaret, tulit Longum murum
CCLXXX stadiis Constantinopoli distantem,
utrumque mare amplexum, barbaros è Ponto,
Colchide, & Mæotide palude incursare fuetos,
arcentem, exstruxit, & quædam in gratiam Euty-
chianorum, de quibus in facris, turbavit. Foris
ipsi cum Longino Zenonis fratre, Bulgaris, Persis,
Barris, Getis, Vitaliano Scytha, Sceuitis Arabibus,
in & Hunnis reserat, Et Longinum quidem, regni
avidum, Isaurorum & Athenodori auxiliissutsul
tum, acievicit; Athenodoro, cujus caput Tharsi
in Cilicia contabuit, interfecto eundem à Prisco
Comite captum, Constantinopoli in theatro cir-
cumdustum, exquisitis Niceæ supplicis, necavit,
& sic bello Isaurico finem imposuit. Bulgaris,
Marcell. gens hastenus ignota, ex Borealibus progrellâ,
Chronic. postquam non tantum Thraciam vastasset, sed
& Anastasii exercitum concidisset, donis mitigati
sunt: pauló post * reduces, muneribus quoque
placati, ut in Pannoniam penetrarent, persuasi
sunt. De Persis in Persarum historia agetur.
Barris, cum Pontum ex condicto invasissent, Anastasium
à persecutione Orthodoxorum averterė.
Eidem cum Bulgaris, astu Getæ, duce Mundone,
Marcell. Thessaliam vastantes, succubuere. Cum enim
Chronic. Sabinianus Consul, contra eos missus, ingenti as-
sectus esset clade, pecunia bellum sopitum est.
Scenitæ Arabes Mefopotamiam & Palæstinam
Cedreno. vastantes ad sædus adegit. Vitalianus Comes,
cui persecutio Orthodoxorum in Anastasium in-
surgendi causa, Scythiâ, Mœsiâ & Thraciâ occu-
patis, Constantinopolin classe obsedit. Anastasius,
cum
Theodor. Lect. 2.

page.notes: Left margin notes: "Marcell. in Chronic.", "Theodor. Lect. 2.", "Cedren." and year marks 492, 497, 498, 499, 502, 503, 514. Right margin marks at the top: "Lib. III. A.C." Marginal references partly illegible; the second sentence printed as above is only partly legible in the scan and some words are uncertain. The Greek "Eutyche" name at line starts is likely printed as Eutyc[?]. Printed text is very faint in places.
